title: OrdersAPI — Create Order
objective: Create an order normally, then create one where the client's own values for server-computed fields simply overwrite what the server just calculated.

verifier.condition: A created order's stored status is 'shipped' or its stored total differs from price times quantity, set directly from the request body after the server computed its own values.

weakness: After computing the order's real total and default status, the handler merges the entire original request body back onto the record, so any field the client supplied — including ones the server just set itself — ends up overwriting the computed value.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /api/orders (server-computed fields are overwritten by a later merge of the raw request body)
seededData: One product, a $80 keyboard, in a fixed catalog. In-memory order store.
hints: Create a normal order and look at its full JSON response — what fields does the server appear to compute itself?
Those same field names are plain JSON properties. What happens if your request body already contains one of them?
An order that was never paid for doesn't usually start out 'shipped'.
burpNotes: Send a normal order creation request to Repeater, then add the server-computed field names directly into your JSON body with your own values.
